newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise then fall on IMF loan hopes.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise then fall on IMF loan hopes.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed but then fell back, except for the fifth tranche, on hopes Russia would receive delayed loan tranches from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), dealers said on Tuesday.

IMF chief representative in Moscow, Tom Wolf, said the IMF's experts had completed their assessment of the Russian economy and had recommended that the IMF board meet on Friday on whether to pay out delayed loan tranches to Russia.
"There has been an attempt to push up prices after the IMF news...The fifth tranche was the only one to stick to the new level," Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said.
Dealers said prices had risen briefly by up to 0.5 point. The 2003 and 2008 maturities were the most actively traded, with resistance levels at 60.50 and 42.70, respectively.
They added a local bank had been seen buying the fifth tranche in the last two days in trading that was otherwise calm ahead of year-end holidays.
"Like on Monday, the fifth tranche was edging up on local buying," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
